messages:
Nico H.: FYI landed a small runtime change on canary tonight for small/med families. End-to-end bench shows median down ~11ms, p95 down ~72ms, p99 down ~190ms, and estimated token-cost drop ~7%. No model weights changed.

deploy-bot: canary deploy 1/4 -> us-east-1 started at 20:02:02 by nico.h; image: runtime:v2026.4.18-sparse-fuse

Priya S.: What did you change broadly?

Nico H.: Two knobs: (1) enabled sparse-attention fusion for short sequences that hit dense blocks, which reduces kernel launch overhead; (2) microbatch coalescer now opportunistically collapses tiny batches when GPU queue depth is low. Both are gated behind runtime flags per-model.

Tom B.: Any regressions on QA/evals?

Nico H.: Ran perf evals (1.2M tokens + curated QA set). No deterministic diffs on the CI anchors. A couple of soft-prob differences on low-confidence tokens but within noise.

Priya S.: How are we monitoring rollback conditions?

Nico H.: Short-circuit rules: automatic rollback if errors > 0.5% absolute over 5m OR p99 exceeds baseline by 12% sustained for 10m. PromQL for p99: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(req_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))`. Also tracking cost delta tile on the canary dashboard.

Tom B.: Can we try a soak on a low-traffic dedicated pool before a full rollout?

Nico H.: Yes planned: 1/4 -> 2/4 -> dedicated-soak-24h -> 50% -> full. Will post soak results in #eng-runtime after 24h.

Priya S.: Awesome. Can you attach the perf CSV to the canary ticket? I'll pull numbers for the weekly update.

Nico H.: Will do. Thanks team :)
